title: Why won't my sourdough rise?
body: My sourdough starter looks active but the dough barely rises during bulk fermentation. The kitchen sits around 18 degrees. Should I proof the dough somewhere warmer, or feed the starter more often before mixing the dough?

title: How often should I feed a sourdough starter?
body: I keep my starter on the counter and feed it once a day. It smells sharp and vinegary. Does an underfed starter make the dough sluggish, and does refrigeration change the feeding schedule?

title: How long should I knead bread dough?
body: I knead the dough by hand for about ten minutes and the gluten still feels weak. The windowpane test tears immediately. Does longer kneading develop gluten, or does the flour matter more than the kneading time?

title: What temperature is best for bulk fermentation?
body: My bread dough ferments very slowly in a cold kitchen. If I raise the dough temperature does the fermentation speed up proportionally, and does warmer fermentation hurt the flavour of the bread?

title: Why is my bread dense with a tight crumb?
body: Every loaf comes out dense with a tight crumb and very little rise. I use bread flour and instant yeast. Is this underproofing, weak gluten, or too little water in the dough?

title: Can I substitute instant yeast for fresh yeast?
body: A bread recipe calls for fresh yeast but I only have instant yeast. What is the conversion, and does the dough need a longer rise or a different fermentation schedule with instant yeast?

title: Does flour protein content change the crumb?
body: Bread flour has more protein than plain flour. Does the extra protein really change the gluten and the crumb, or does hydration matter more? My loaf is dense with either flour.

title: How do I shape a loaf without deflating the dough?
body: When I shape the dough after bulk fermentation I knock all the gas out and the loaf never recovers its rise during the final proof. Is there a gentler way to shape wet dough?

title: Why do I need steam for oven spring?
body: Recipes say to add steam when the bread goes into the oven. Without steam my crust sets early and the loaf gets almost no oven spring. How much steam does a home oven actually need?

title: Is an overnight cold retard worth it?
body: I read that retarding the dough overnight in the fridge improves flavour. Does the cold fermentation actually develop flavour, or does it just make the dough easier to shape and score?

title: What hydration should pizza dough be?
body: My pizza dough tears when I stretch it. Higher hydration dough sounds right but it sticks to everything. Does more water help the gluten relax, or do I need a longer bulk fermentation?

title: What angle should I sharpen a kitchen knife to?
body: I sharpen my chef knife on a whetstone but I cannot hold a consistent angle. Is twenty degrees per side right for a European knife, and does a shallower angle dull faster?

title: Does a honing steel actually sharpen a knife?
body: I run my knife over a honing steel before every use and it feels sharper. Does honing remove metal like a whetstone does, or does it only straighten the edge?

title: How do I stop a carbon steel knife rusting?
body: My carbon steel knife develops rust spots overnight even after I dry it. Does an oiled edge help, and does the patina on an older knife actually protect the steel underneath?

title: Wooden or plastic cutting board for knife edges?
body: I was told a wooden cutting board is gentler on a knife edge than plastic. Does the board material really change how quickly the edge dulls, or is that a myth?

title: Why does my knife go dull so quickly?
body: I sharpen my knife on a whetstone and within a week the edge is dull again. Is the steel too soft, is my sharpening angle wrong, or is the cutting board the problem?

title: My oven runs hot at 350 degrees
body: An oven thermometer reads 375 when I set the dial to 350. Should I calibrate the oven or just subtract the difference every time I bake? Baking at 350 comes out overdone.

title: How do I convert 180 to a convection setting?
body: A recipe says 180 in a conventional oven. For convection do I drop the temperature by 20 degrees to 160, or shorten the baking time instead? Some recipes say 220 for bread.

title: How long should a pizza stone preheat?
body: I preheat the pizza stone at 250 for half an hour and the base still comes out pale. Does the stone need longer, or does the oven need to be hotter for a pizza base?

title: Is an oven thermometer worth buying?
body: My baking results vary a lot between recipes. Would an oven thermometer tell me anything the dial does not, and how far off is a typical domestic oven at 200 degrees?

title: Do I need to brine a turkey?
body: A wet brine means you soak the poultry in salt water overnight. Does it help?

title: Should I brine chicken breast?
body: A wet brine means you soak the poultry in salt water for hours. Worth it?

title: How long should I brine a whole chicken?
body: You soak the poultry in a salt brine, but how long before the texture turns spongy?

title: Is a dry brine better than a wet brine?
body: Instead of a soak you rub salt onto the poultry and leave it uncovered.

title: Can I brine a frozen turkey?
body: If the poultry is frozen does the salt brine soak in at all, or must it thaw first?

title: How much salt goes into a brine?
body: Recipes vary wildly. Does the poultry soak up more salt from a stronger brine?

title: Should I rinse poultry after brining?
body: After the soak the surface tastes very salty. Does rinsing undo the brine?

title: Can I reuse a brine?
body: The salt brine looks fine after one soak. Is reusing it on more poultry safe?

title: Does brining make poultry rubbery?
body: My brined chicken has a spongy texture. Did the poultry soak in the salt brine too long?

title: Do you brine pork the same way as poultry?
body: A pork loin dries out. Does the same salt brine and soak work as it does for poultry?
